elasticity.definition: Relative perplexity increase per relative cache reduction, per matched pair. Reported as a distribution rather than a pooled slope because a pooled slope in perplexity-per-megabyte is dominated by the largest architectures: least squares weights by the square of the saving, and the same six perplexity points are one per cent of 509 and ten per cent of 60. The absolute slope is kept above for continuity and should not be read as the answer.

what_the_slope_means: Perplexity given up for each megabyte of key-value cache removed, at matched head count and depth and width. Positive means the saving costs quality; near zero means grouped-query attention is close to free, which is the claim the technique is usually adopted on.
why_matched: kv is not independent of the rest: it must divide h, and architectures with many heads can reach cache reductions that few-headed ones cannot. Comparing across unmatched architectures measures the correlation between kv and everything kv is constrained by. Matching is on every gene but kv — leaving the feed-forward ratio free was enough to bury the effect entirely.
